setup.description: Fixture repo`): libgit2 in a fresh temp dir, one committed file tracked.txt = 'original\n' (message 'initial').

steps: overwrite tracked.txt on disk with 'rewritten by the agent\n' (simulating an AI edit)
write a new file new.txt = 'created by the agent\n' (simulating an AI-created file)
cases.notes: changed_paths/restore's touched-path list is sorted alphabetically (diff_paths sorts). new.txt has no entry in the checkpoint's tree, so restore deletes it rather than writing anything; tracked.txt's blob from the checkpoint's tree is written back verbatim. Confirms restore never touches the index or HEAD (GIT-024) — only working-tree file content.

setup.description: Same base fixture as restore-reverts-edits-and-deletes-created-files: tracked.txt = 'original\n' committed.

steps: write staged.txt = 'staged content\n' and stage it (index.add_path + index.write) — this is the real on-disk .git/index, not the checkpoint's in-memory one
write untracked.txt = 'untracked content\n' without staging it
read the real repo index's path list
delete untracked.txt from disk; overwrite staged.txt on disk with 'clobbered\n'
cases.notes: Proves create()'s snapshot_tree builds a brand-new libgit2 attached only to its own in-process Repository handle (repo.set_index) — the real on-disk index used for staging is never read or written by checkpoint creation, so it still shows exactly [staged.txt, tracked.txt] afterward. Both the staged file and the untracked file were captured in the snapshot (statuses() with include_untracked reports both), so restoring after clobbering/deleting them on disk puts back their checkpoint-time content for both, regardless of staged-vs-untracked status.

setup.description: Same base fixture: tracked.txt = 'original\n' committed, no further edits made before or after checkpoint creation.

cases.notes: Nothing changed the working tree between create() and remove_if_unchanged(), so diff_paths(repo, commit) is empty and the checkpoint is deleted immediately — used by the Claude command's post-AI-run cleanup (05-ai-engines.md) so a run that touched nothing leaves no undo entry for the user to see.
